objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: From the hodor foothold, enumerate Active Directory over LDAP: recover svc_backup's password from its description attribute, confirm the nested group path (IT Backup -> Vault Readers), then read flag.txt from the //dc/vault share that only Vault Readers may open.
hints: hodor is a normal domain user (hodor / Hodor123!), and any authenticated user may read most of AD over LDAP. Point your resolver at the DC and bind with a plain simple bind: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<dc> -D 'hodor@north.sevenkingdoms.local' -w 'Hodor123!' -b 'DC=north,DC=sevenkingdoms,DC=local' '(objectClass=user)' sAMAccountName description memberOf.
Read the object attributes, not just the names: one service account (svc_backup) has its own password sitting in its description attribute. Administrators do this far too often.

svc_backup is not a direct member of the group that unlocks the vault. Map the group memberships (nxc ldap <dc> -u hodor -p 'Hodor123!' --bloodhound --collection All, or follow memberOf by hand): svc_backup -> IT Backup -> Vault Readers. The vault share is restricted to Vault Readers, so authenticate as svc_backup: smbclient //dc/vault -U 'NORTH\svc_backup%<leaked>' -c 'get flag.txt'.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What is the name of the activity where an authenticated user reads Active Directory over LDAP to map users, groups and attributes?

steps.title: Find the leaky account
steps.prompt: Which service account leaks its own password in Active Directory? (username)

steps.title: Name the attribute
steps.prompt: Which object attribute holds the leaked password? (one word)

steps.title: Follow the nested group
steps.prompt: svc_backup is a direct member of which group that is itself nested inside Vault Readers? (group name)

steps.title: Name the gated resource
steps.prompt: Which group must you belong to in order to open the share that holds the flag? (group name)
